units.name: 61 Self Definition
units.passage: Most of us assume that we must first change how we see ourselves before we can act differently, but the reverse often works better: intentionally altering what we do is a powerful way to build a new picture of who we are. Suppose I keep having relaxed, easy conversations with strangers at social gatherings, or I feel my energy rising as I speak in front of a crowded lecture hall. Each time this happens, my image of myself shifts a little. The shift takes place both in my awareness and beneath it. Below the surface, my adaptive mind quietly concludes from my behavior that I must be a sociable person, and that conclusion soon finds its way into the story I consciously tell about myself. Once my self-image has moved in this direction, acting in outgoing ways no longer requires a struggle; it begins to happen on its own. A self that runs automatically generates behavior that runs automatically too. In this way, my newly sociable self takes the wheel, guiding me toward choices I would once have avoided, such as striking up a warm conversation with the stranger beside me on a flight instead of hiding behind a novel.

units.name: 62 Evolution Study
units.passage: Fossils tell us a great deal about creatures that lived long ago, yet because the fossil record is full of missing pieces, scientists struggle to trace exactly how one form of life turned into another. A more direct approach would be to watch evolution happen by tracking every genetic change from one generation to the next. For that, researchers first need a suitable living subject. Bacteria are the natural candidate, since they grow easily in lab dishes and multiply at remarkable speed. Consider the difference in timescales: an evolutionary study of people would require waiting about 26 years, on average, for each new generation, whereas E. coli, one of the most thoroughly researched bacteria, produces a fresh generation roughly every 20 minutes. On top of that, E. coli carries a relatively compact genome, so tracing the real genetic changes in each generation costs far less time and money. Taking advantage of these traits, scientists are able to watch and even control evolution as it unfolds, which sheds light on how evolution actually works.

units.name: 63 Public Transport
units.passage: A truly advanced nation is not one in which even low-income families own cars; rather, it is one in which wealthy people choose to ride buses and trains. Building sustainable city transportation and well-connected public transit systems unquestionably brings about a fundamental rise in the quality of people's lives. Good transit opens the way to shops and workplaces, to schools and hospitals, to recreation, and to whatever residents require for daily living. It also benefits public health: people who rely on public transportation tend to walk more, which makes them fitter and, as a result, eases the burden placed on medical systems. At the same time, a sustainable urban network has two tasks. It should reduce the unwanted consequences of traffic, such as congestion, polluted air, and accidents, and it should also give low-income and vulnerable citizens greater freedom to move around. In the end, the success of such a system depends on how far the whole city can be reached by every one of its inhabitants.

items.exp: 대중교통망의 발전이 삶의 질을 근본적으로 높인다고 하고, 그 성공은 모든 주민이 도시 전체에 얼마나 접근할 수 있는지에 달려 있다고 했어요.

units.name: 64 Managing Emotions
units.passage: When emotions are running high, hardly anyone can see a situation clearly. People who have had an exciting experience usually rush to repeat it without stopping to judge whether it was actually good for them. On the other hand, people who have lived through something painful often go to great lengths to stay away from anything similar, and this avoidance can leave them emotionally tangled. In both cases, careful reflection allows you to put some space between yourself and the strong feelings attached to unusually wonderful or terrible moments, so that you can look at them anew. Reflection means withdrawing from the instant grip of your feelings in order to review what happened objectively and clearly. Through it, you can reconsider past excitement with emotional maturity and study painful events with reason and honesty. Such a process helps people let go of the heavy emotional load they have been dragging along. A feeling that survives honest examination and lasts over time possesses emotional integrity, and that kind of feeling deserves your full commitment.

units.name: 65 Learning Strategy
units.passage: Most of us have met a person who seems to have a reply ready for every possible question. A good example is Cliff Clavin, the know-it-all mail carrier on the television comedy Cheers, who apparently could never bring himself to admit that he did not know something. This urge to always supply an answer is not just a quirk of one fictional character; it affects all of us, and it gets in the way of real learning. The reason is that our society has built entire systems designed to judge and rank answers, and in schools these systems take the form of grades at every stage of education. Imagine, instead, a system that evaluated and rewarded the finest questions. Picture teachers and leaders holding meetings where people's questions were carefully heard, and where the most valuable ones were recognized and then put into action. Would such a setting create fresh possibilities and allow learning to thrive? I am convinced it would. However, we will never head that way as long as we believe that learning and knowing are mainly about having the right answers.

items.exp: 필자는 정답에 대한 집착이 배움을 방해한다고 하며, 가장 좋은 질문을 평가하고 인정하는 체계가 있다면 배움이 번성할 것이라고 주장해요.

The Secret to Answering Every Question

units.name: 66 Gaming and Addiction
units.passage: Better graphics, richer sound, more lifelike worlds, faster downloads, and the chance to play anywhere at any moment on a phone have all made video games harder than ever to put down. Douglas Gentile, a distinguished psychology professor at Iowa State University, argues that access is clearly one of the central causes of every kind of addiction. As he explained to an interviewer, people cannot become hooked on a game that their device does not offer them. Because games now appear, in his words, on nearly every screen surrounding us, he expects compulsive gaming to keep spreading. In fact, the game industry has openly aimed over the past ten years to turn gaming into something present in everyone's life, a habit and even an addiction shared by the general public. Its strategy has been to move beyond the limited pool of devoted players and reach the mainstream entertainment market. As Cammie Dunaway, an executive at Nintendo, once put it, the goal is to sell to a wider audience instead of selling ever more to a small group.

게임 업계는 열성적인 소수 이용자에게 집중해야 한다.
휴대 기기는 게임보다 학습에 더 많이 쓰인다.
items.exp: 어디서나 게임을 할 수 있게 된 접근성이 중독의 핵심 요인이며, 업계도 게임을 모두의 습관으로 만드는 것을 목표로 해 왔다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 지문의 [compulsive]의 영영 풀이로 가장 알맞은 것은?

enjoyed for a short time

choices: to stop playing

units.name: 67 Mathematics and Technology
units.passage: Forecasting is one of the services that mathematics provides. Because they grasped how the planets and moons move, astronomers were able to tell in advance when eclipses of the Sun and Moon would occur, when a comet would reappear, and where an asteroid would be after it had slipped behind the Sun and could no longer be observed. Yet mathematics does far more than predict. When you know the workings of a system, you need not simply watch it from the sidelines; you can try to steer it so that it behaves the way you wish. Such control can be seen everywhere, from the thermostat that holds a boiler at a steady temperature to the systems that manage traffic lights in a busy city. Electronic pacemakers, which regulate the heartbeat of patients with heart problems, offer another case. The space shuttle, too, depends on a highly sophisticated mathematical control system; without it, the craft would drop like a brick, since no human pilot could react fast enough to fix the instabilities built into its design. Still, we should keep our ambitions modest. Controlling the weather, for instance, remains at an early stage: even when rain clouds are around, we cannot produce rain with much reliability.

units.name: 68 Mindset Shift
units.passage: It may be difficult to admit that time itself lies behind your pain and hardship. Most of us blame particular events or conditions in our lives, and from an ordinary point of view, that explanation seems correct. However, as long as you have not faced the mind's deepest flaw, its habit of clinging to the past and the future while refusing the present moment, one hardship can simply be swapped for another. Imagine that every difficulty you now blame for your misery vanished overnight as if by magic. If you had not grown more present and more aware, you would before long find a fresh collection of troubles, much like a gloomy cloud that trails you everywhere. In the end, there is really just one problem, and it sits at the heart of how we think: the mind that is bound to time. Time cannot offer a solution, and freedom will never arrive at some future moment. Because presence opens the door to freedom, now is the only time you can be free. We naturally assume that our suffering comes from feeling powerless in certain situations, but its true root is our inability to live in the present.

units.name: 69 Meaning Transformation
units.passage: At first, the word "revolution" referred to the steady, repeating motion of bodies in space, such as the Earth's yearly journey around the Sun. Once people began to apply it to society, as in political revolutions, however, its sense shifted. Rather than naming the regular, foreseeable cycles of the stars, the word came to mean sudden, sweeping change brought about through force and the destruction of the established system. This new interpretation of the word reveals an interesting irony. Although revolutionaries dream of complete and fundamental change, the way societies develop tends to move in circles, which implies that history may in fact repeat itself just as the heavenly bodies keep returning along their paths in the sky. So while revolutionaries may see themselves as people driving a process that marks the final collapse of the old order and gives birth to a new world, what they do may in the end obey the same repeating patterns that rule the movements of the stars.

units.name: 70 Algorithm
units.passage: When decisions are left to algorithms, existing prejudices can be copied, and this may deepen the disadvantages that certain groups already face. One of the best-known examples of such bias in hiring comes from Amazon. From 2014 to 2017, the company tried to create an automated tool that could pick out the strongest job applicants. The program learned from ten years of the company's own hiring records, and because men had long made up a large share of workers in the technology field, it reportedly came to favor male candidates and to rate women lower, treating men as the ideal hires. The company's engineers worked to fix the flaw, but they could not correct it satisfactorily, so the project was eventually dropped. In general, a company must answer for its hiring choices no matter how they are reached or who, or what, reaches them. For this reason, it is crucial that every algorithm a company builds, along with the data used to train it, be tested carefully to make sure it is suitable for the job it is meant to do.

units.name: 71 Literacy
units.passage: Risk literacy differs from the basic ability to read and write because it demands an emotional shift: we must give up the reassuring voice of authority and the false belief that things are certain, and instead learn to accept responsibility and to cope with uncertainty. Unfortunately, we have not come very far. Research shows that most patients prefer to trust their doctors' knowledge without question and are too timid to request proof, yet they leave appointments feeling fully informed. In the same way, even after the financial crisis, many bank customers still put unquestioning faith in their advisors, risking their savings in meetings shorter than a football match. Plenty of people hold on to the idea that the future can be foretold, and some even pay fortune-tellers for a sense of certainty that is not real. Each autumn, famous financial firms announce their predictions for the coming year, and we pour $200 billion a year into a forecasting business whose forecasts are mostly wrong. Teachers and political leaders, then, need to recognize risk literacy as an essential subject for this century. Instead of being pressured to follow what experts think is best, people should be prepared to make well-grounded choices on their own.

units.name: 72 Scientific Breakthroughs
units.passage: It is a mistake to demand that fresh ideas in mathematics and science pay off in money right away. Turning a mathematical insight into a product that a factory can manufacture or a family can use at home usually requires a long time, often as much as a hundred years. In the 1600s, scholars were fascinated by the way violin strings vibrate, and three centuries afterward this curiosity led researchers to identify radio waves and later to build radio, radar, and television, all of which are commercially valuable. Perhaps the journey could have been somewhat shorter, but not by a great deal. Many people in our society believe that scientific progress can be accelerated if researchers aim only at practical uses and set aside research driven by pure curiosity, but they are mistaken. Research aimed at specific goals produces nothing but safe, foreseeable, short-term outcomes, and whatever you can foresee, your rivals can foresee as well. Chasing only safe projects will leave all of us poorer. Truly significant breakthroughs can never be predicted, and that unpredictability is exactly what gives them their value: they transform our world in ways nobody expected.

units.name: 73 Comfort Zone
units.passage: In a world full of pressure, the routines we know well feel deeply comforting, so it may sound almost offensive when someone advises us to give them up and accept even more stress. Yet that is precisely the issue. When you keep repeating the same safe habits, you stop moving forward, and in a world that keeps speeding up, standing in one place actually means slipping behind. This does not mean you must throw away every comfortable routine you have. You only need to let go of the ones that keep you from growing. One example is delaying tasks you dislike, such as asking your teacher for extra days to finish homework. Another is steering clear of conflict; giving in when you truly care about an issue is, in effect, abandoning yourself. A third is resisting change, which is risky because the learning environment never stops shifting, and those who fail to adjust are left behind. Fortunately, stepping out of these comfort zones is likely to bring fresh opportunities and fewer of the problems you once dreaded facing. It might even lead you to a workable, bearable "neutral zone" that you can handle calmly.

units.name: 74 Business Ethics
units.passage: Only a few decades ago, universities offered no classes with titles such as "Business Ethics." Most people assumed that the two words simply could not go together. Business, in their view, existed to earn as much profit as possible, whereas ethics meant assisting others out of pure generosity. Today, however, ethical conduct is regarded as a marketing strategy that companies can hardly do without, since it helps them sell more. Almost every large corporation now runs at least one Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program. Two expressions frequently linked to such programs are "greenwashing" and "whitewashing." The first describes firms that overstate how good their goods or operations are for the environment, and the second describes comparable tricks concerning social or moral matters. Even so, we should not hastily write off every corporate promise of social and ethical responsibility as mere greenwashing or propaganda. This is particularly true now that the Internet and social media allow skeptical consumers to reveal such misleading efforts much more easily than before.

units.name: 75 Stereotype
units.passage: According to Caryn Park, an education researcher, even preschoolers notice differences in race and ethnicity, and they build opinions about them using whatever information their social surroundings provide. Her research indicated that when no older or more knowledgeable person is around, young children tend to work together to interpret ideas, such as race and ethnicity, that lie beyond what they can yet grasp. Park pointed out that when children teach one another about these differences, they may end up holding mistaken beliefs, so teachers have a duty to guide their understanding of human diversity with care. Nobody enters the world holding prejudices; rather, children gradually absorb stereotypes from the grown-ups and the media that surround them as they get older. For those of us who teach young children, the words we choose and the remarks we make can greatly shape how they view differences among people. Therefore, when discussing such differences, we should rely on an anti-bias approach and speak with accuracy, calmness, and respect.

units.name: 76 Public Relations (PR)
units.passage: The legal fight that pitted Ben & Jerry's against Häagen-Dazs shows that opportunities can be found where you least expect them and turned to your benefit. Häagen-Dazs was supported by Pillsbury, one of the most powerful players in the food business, but Ben & Jerry's refused to be intimidated by this. Instead, it presented the lawsuit as a David and Goliath tale: two owners of a small business being pushed around by a heartless corporate giant. Before long, major newspapers and magazines were running feature articles about the dispute. The conflict was finally resolved by 1987. Yet what mattered more than winning in court was the huge publicity advantage Ben & Jerry's gained. Many thousands of consumers who had never heard of the brand began to ask why Pillsbury wanted to hold back the small company's ice cream. In their eyes, Häagen-Dazs was attacking American tradition, family values, and the spirit of entrepreneurship. In this way, the company made lemonade out of lemons, turning a difficult situation into a valuable chance.

items.exp: Ben & Jerry's가 거대 기업과의 소송이라는 불리한 상황을 큰 홍보 효과로 바꾼 사례로, 예상치 못한 곳에서 기회를 잡을 수 있다는 내용이에요.

units.name: 77 Intuitive Judgement
units.passage: When we face an unfamiliar problem and have no idea how to deal with it, or when time is simply too short, we tend to trust our intuition. Rather than examining the situation carefully and weighing different options, intuition jumps to a quick solution. It searches through our stored experiences for an earlier problem that looks much the same. That old problem then acts as a model, and the new one is "solved" by following the same pattern. In everyday life, this quick method usually works well, but it breaks down when chance plays a role. Imagine being asked which is more probable: rolling at least one six when you throw a die six times, or rolling at least two sixes when you throw it twelve times. Most people feel that the two results are equally likely, since the second simply doubles the first. In fact, however, the second outcome is less likely. Such a surprising answer goes against our instincts because we know countless cases in which things grow in proportion. When probability is involved, though, relying on that sense of proportion can lead us to wrong conclusions.

units.name: 78 Complex Systems
units.passage: Many puzzles in chemistry, biology, environmental studies, and the human sciences are still unsolved, but not because our knowledge of subatomic physics is lacking. The real reason is that researchers have yet to discover the patterns, structures, and connections that appear at higher levels of organization. Studying only atoms or the particles inside them cannot explain why a wave crashes on the shore or how an insect acts. Consider the albatross, which can travel thousands of miles across the Southern Ocean and still find its way back to its nest with great reliability. No one could ever predict such behavior, not even in theory, by treating the bird as a mere collection of atoms. Likewise, mapping the human genome, which revealed the chain of molecules carrying our inherited traits, ranks among the most remarkable scientific feats of recent years. However, it is only the opening act of a much bigger task for post-genomic science: figuring out how genetic information sets off the building of proteins and shows itself as an embryo develops.

units.name: 79 Skills
units.passage: Take an honest look at the abilities you already have. Figure out which areas are your strengths and which ones badly need work, and deal with the weakest ones before anything else. This is tougher than it appears, as most worthwhile habits tend to be, yet there is no other route to real growth. In his classic The Book of Five Rings, Miyamoto Musashi, a famous Japanese swordsman of the 1500s, gave this advice: "Never have a favorite weapon." Fighters understood that they had to keep widening their range of techniques so that their opponents could not guess their next move. The same principle applies to creative work, even though failure there rarely costs anyone their life. Think of a photographer who is comfortable using both small and large cameras and who can shoot under studio lighting as well as out on the street; such a person has greatly expanded the paths along which a career can grow. In the same way, a novelist who also writes excellent short stories has more ways to shape a tale than a writer who has only ever worked in the short form and never tried the longer one.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? "Fighters understood that they had to keep ___ their range of techniques so that their opponents could not guess their next move."

widening

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

items.q: 밑줄 친 [Never have a favorite weapon]이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (In his classic The Book of Five Rings, Miyamoto Musashi, a famous Japanese swordsman of the 1500s, gave this advice: "Never have a favorite weapon.")

a novelist who also [writes] excellent short stories

units.name: 80 Biodiversity
units.passage: Why should we bother to protect rare, threatened species that offer people no obvious benefit? The answer is that even minor species usually play parts in a web of complicated relationships with numerous other organisms, and some of these roles can turn out to matter greatly for ecosystems or for evolution. Consider the dodo, along with the Carolina parakeet. Both birds once carried seeds across wide areas, and since they died out, the makeup of the forests where they lived has changed for good. Likewise, many uncommon insects pollinate only a narrow range of plants, so when those insects vanish, the plants struggle to reproduce and survive. Over the long span of evolutionary time, our understanding of what happens after a rare species disappears is even weaker. Still, we are sure that, as time passes, evolution can strengthen the influence one species has on whether others survive. In most situations, scientists lack the biological knowledge needed to forecast exactly what the loss of a rare species will bring. Yet one thing is certain: when a species is gone, nothing can ever fully replace it.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 인간에게 쓸모없는 희귀종은 굳이 보호할 필요가 없다.
멸종이 생태계에 미치는 영향은 과학으로 정확히 예측할 수 있다.
희귀종도 생태적·진화적으로 중요한 역할을 할 수 있고 한번 사라지면 대체할 수 없으므로 보존해야 한다.
새는 곤충보다 생태계 유지에 더 중요한 역할을 한다.
진화는 시간이 지날수록 희귀종의 영향을 약하게 만든다.
items.exp: 희귀종이 다른 종과의 상호작용 속에서 중요한 역할을 할 수 있고, 사라지면 완전히 대체할 수 없다는 것이 글의 요지예요.

choices: 도도새와 캐롤라이나앵무는 씨앗을 퍼뜨리는 역할을 했다.
두 새가 사라진 뒤 숲의 구조는 곧 원래대로 회복되었다.
희귀 곤충은 대부분 여러 종류의 식물을 가리지 않고 수분한다.
진화적 시간 척도에서의 멸종 영향은 비교적 잘 알려져 있다.
과학자들은 대부분의 경우 희귀종 멸종의 결과를 정확히 예측할 수 있다.
items.exp: 두 새가 넓은 지역에 씨앗을 옮겼다(carried seeds across wide areas)고 했어요. 숲의 구조는 영원히 바뀌었다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에 따르면 희귀 곤충이 사라지면 일어나는 일로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 인간의 식량이 즉시 부족해진다.
새들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨리지 못하게 된다.
숲이 이전보다 더 빽빽해진다.
다른 곤충이 곧바로 그 역할을 대신한다.
그 곤충이 수분하던 식물이 번식하고 살아남기 어려워진다.
items.exp: 희귀 곤충은 좁은 범위의 식물만 수분하므로, 사라지면 그 식물이 번식하고 생존하기 힘들어진다고 했어요.

choices: to remember something from the past
to say what will probably happen in the future
to stop something from happening
to describe something in great detail
to change the result of something

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? "In most situations, scientists lack the biological knowledge ___ to forecast exactly what the loss of a rare species will bring."

needing

needed

items.q: 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Life and Death of the Dodo
How Insects Pollinate Plants
Predicting Extinction with Modern Science
Evolution Makes Rare Species Unnecessary
Why Even Rare Species Deserve Protection

because they provide obvious benefits to humans
because they are easy for scientists to study
because they take part in a complex web of relationships with other organisms
because they can be quickly replaced by similar species
items.exp: 'even minor species usually play parts in a web of complicated relationships with numerous other organisms'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Although scientists usually cannot (A) ___ the exact results of losing a rare species, such species often play hidden roles in ecosystems, and once they are gone they are (B) ___.

protect
study
forget
predict

units.name: 81 Social Connections
units.passage: Our drive to connect with others is rooted so deeply in us that being cut off from people can cloud our thinking, since social ties have helped build human intelligence in the first place. Most brain scientists today accept that our species became what it is largely because we had to cope with one another. A recent study even indicates that loneliness can change the way DNA is read in the cells that make up our immune system. Through these and countless other routes, feeling connected, or feeling alone, has a powerful effect not only on how we act but also on how our bodies work. Everyone's body weakens with age at some point, yet loneliness can make that decline much steeper. On the other hand, strong and healthy relationships can slow down the same process. When we reach a state of high social well-being, which is within reach for every one of us, we enjoy healing benefits that help us stay active and strong for a longer time.

items.q: 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Loneliness: A Harmless Feeling
How Intelligence Develops Without Others
Why Older People Feel Lonely
Social Bonds: Good for the Mind and the Body
The Secret of DNA in Brain Cells
items.exp: 사회적 유대가 사고력, 면역 세포, 신체 노화에 영향을 주고 건강한 관계는 회복 효과가 있다는 내용이므로 사회적 유대가 정신과 몸 모두에 이롭다는 제목이 알맞아요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

최근 연구에 따르면 외로움은 뇌세포 속 DNA가 읽히는 방식을 바꾼다.
연결감이나 외로움은 행동과 신체 모두에 영향을 준다.
외로움은 나이에 따른 신체 쇠퇴를 더 가파르게 만들 수 있다.
높은 사회적 웰빙 상태는 누구나 도달할 수 있다.

인간 지능이 형성되는 과정
사회적 웰빙에 도달하는 과정
인간관계가 깊어지는 과정
나이가 들면서 몸이 약해지는 과정

choices: what
which
that
how
where

the effects of social connection and loneliness on mind and body
the history of brain science
ways to make new friends quickly

items.q: According to the passage, what happens when people reach a state of high social well-being?

They enjoy healing benefits that help them stay active and strong longer.
Their DNA is completely rewritten.
They become less intelligent.
Their bodies stop aging altogether.

Because human intelligence itself grew out of social ties, being (A) ___ harms both our thinking and our bodies, while close relationships help (B) ___ the physical decline of aging.

units.name: 82 How to Read
units.passage: Many readers skip over a book's title and preface, and one reason is that they see no value in identifying what type of book they have in hand. In doing so, they ignore the very first principle of reading a book analytically. If they made an effort to apply that principle, they would appreciate the help the author offers. Clearly, writers believe readers ought to understand what sort of book they are holding. This is why authors take pains to state it clearly in the preface and generally try to make the title, or the subtitle at least, tell the reader something about the content. Einstein and Infeld, for instance, wrote in their introduction to The Evolution of Physics that readers should realize a popular science book is still not to be read the way one reads a novel. Beyond this, authors put together a thorough table of contents so that readers can learn about the details of the explanation ahead of time. In any case, the chapter titles printed at the beginning of a book work to expand the meaning of the main title.

feel physical pain

act carelessly
pretend to agree

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? "In any case, the chapter titles ___ at the beginning of a book work to expand the meaning of the main title."

printing
to print
printed
are printed

units.name: 83 Manufacturing Excellence
units.passage: As competition in the marketplace grows fiercer, manufacturers are under more and more pressure to keep quality under control, which makes testing absolutely central to guaranteeing good products and a well-managed production line. In my view, no other part of manufacturing is as likely to cause disputes as testing. Think about how much depends on it. Testing is how a company confirms that its products satisfy the required specifications and that its processes are running as they should. When test results are flawed or doubtful, huge sums of money are put in danger. A single wrong judgment made during a test can lead to costly rework, wasted materials, delayed shipments, unhappy customers, and lost sales. There is one principle that every sound quality philosophy should include: you cannot test quality into a product. I have often heard people say, "Maybe the product failed only because the test was done poorly. If we run the test once more, perhaps it will pass." However, improving the way a product is tested does not improve the product itself. For these reasons, we work hard to make sure that our testing procedures are accurate, our instruments are properly calibrated, our staff are thoroughly trained, and our sampling plans are reliable.

units.name: 84 Heredity
units.passage: Individual genes appear to have surprisingly little to do with shaping the large-scale traits of human beings, meaning the features we can actually see. Apart from a handful of clear cases such as eye and hair color, almost no direct tie exists between a particular gene and a visible trait. Height offers a good illustration. Nobody seriously doubts that our genes strongly influence how tall we grow, since tall parents usually produce tall children. It is therefore not surprising that, among all human traits studied so far, height has shown the strongest link to whether a single gene is present or not, setting aside hair color and similar features. What is surprising, though, is how small that one gene's effect on height turns out to be. It explains a mere two percent of the differences in height among people. And that tiny figure represents the "largest" connection ever found between one gene and a human trait.

units.name: 85 Another Person's Shoes
units.passage: Knowing that we ought to feel empathy is easy; actually practicing it is a different matter entirely. There is nothing new or radical about this idea. Since childhood, we have all heard the familiar advice to treat others the way we ourselves wish to be treated. Why, then, do we find it so difficult to pause and imagine life from someone else's position? One possible answer is that the stereotypes we keep in our minds work like a security blanket: deep down, they make us feel safe and comfortable. Labeling people is far simpler than getting to know them. We quickly assume that sports fans must be full of energy, that people who love books must be shy and quiet, and that those passionate about technology must lack social skills. Treating each person as a unique individual takes much more effort, even though that person would hate being reduced to a flat, two-dimensional label just as much as we would. In fact, if all of us made a sincere and constant effort to view the world through other people's eyes, the bullying that surrounds us could disappear almost overnight.

units.name: 86 Works of Art
units.passage: Truly great art earns its greatness for one reason: anyone can approach it and grasp its meaning. When the biblical tale of Joseph is rendered in Chinese, Chinese readers are deeply touched, and we in turn are stirred by the life of the Buddha. Architecture, painting, sculpture, and music work in exactly the same way. So when a work leaves us cold, we should not blame the audience for failing to understand it; instead, we are entitled, and indeed obliged, to decide that the work is either poor art or no art at all. Intellectual activity is different. It demands preparation and a fixed order of study, which is why no one can learn trigonometry before mastering geometry. Art, however, reaches people regardless of how educated or developed they are. Seen this way, the true task of art is to make clear and approachable what would remain obscure and out of reach if it were presented as intellectual knowledge. That is why, when people encounter genuine art, they often feel as if they had always known what it expressed but had simply never found the words for it.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 예술을 제대로 감상하려면 체계적인 사전 교육이 반드시 필요하다.

감동을 주지 못하는 작품은 관객의 이해력 부족 때문에 실패한 것이다.
위대한 예술은 교육 수준과 상관없이 누구에게나 이해되고 감동을 준다.
items.exp: 위대한 예술은 누구나 다가가 이해할 수 있기 때문에 위대하며, 교육·발달 정도와 무관하게 사람에게 닿는다는 것이 요지예요.

units.name: 87 Workplace Management
units.passage: Workers seldom notice it, but they depend heavily on the physical space around them for key information and signals. This reliance connects to the idea of transactive memory, in which people make up for the weaknesses of their own memory and their limited ability to handle information by drawing on systems around them. Colleagues, for instance, serve as devices that store, find, and process information for one another. In much the same way, a sticky note attached to the edge of a computer screen or a document left in a particular tray can act as an extension of a person's memory. People come to rely on coworkers for knowledge, and they can likewise come to rely on features of their physical setting to get their jobs done. Taken too far, however, this reliance can hold groups back, especially those that cannot function outside the special limits of their own workspace. A move to a new office or a shift to remote work may upset the routines and productivity a team has grown used to. For this reason, it is essential to recognize this dependence and handle it wisely in any kind of workplace.

units.name: 88 Architectural Design
units.passage: When architects fail to design places where people feel at ease, their failure reflects a broader human weakness: we struggle to find happiness in many other parts of life as well. Ultimately, poor buildings result as much from flawed psychology as from flawed design. They are simply one more sign of the same habits that cause us to make friends with the wrong people, take jobs that do not suit us, and plan vacations that disappoint us. At the root of these habits lies our everyday failure to know ourselves and to figure out what would truly make us content. Thus, in building, as in those other areas, we reach for quick fixes, so we demolish old streets when what they really need is decent sanitation and better lighting. In contrast, the places we admire as beautiful are created by a small number of architects who are humble enough to question themselves honestly about what they want and determined enough to turn their ideas into well-reasoned plans. Together, these qualities allow them to build spaces that meet needs we were never even aware of having.

items.exp: 'our everyday failure to know ourselves'가 뿌리이고, 좋은 건축가는 'question themselves honestly about what they want'한다고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [we reach for quick fixes]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Thus, in building, as in those other areas, we reach for quick fixes, so we demolish old streets when what they really need is decent sanitation and better lighting.)
choices: 문제를 근본적으로 해결하는 데 시간을 들인다
전문가의 도움을 빠르게 구한다
오래된 것을 고치는 기술을 익힌다
결정을 최대한 미룬다
손쉽고 성급한 해결책에 의존한다

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

take jobs that do not [suit] us
plan vacations that [disappoint] us

units.name: 89 Creativity Enhancement
units.passage: The American artist Georgia O'Keeffe, famous for her huge paintings of flowers, once remarked that truly seeing a flower requires time. The same holds true for composing a poem, and for allowing our own creativity to emerge. That time, however, must be protected from the countless distractions we so readily let control our days. When I first began to write, I discovered that writing and eating lunch with others simply did not mix. Once my work had gained momentum, a break for a meal would end my writing for the rest of the day. I had spent years in real estate, a field in which business lunches were routine, so I was forced to alter my habits and begin turning down lunch meetings and numerous other invitations. By making my working life simpler, I gave my creativity room to grow. Creative work resembles a steam engine: getting its wheels to turn demands enormous inner energy and resources. So if there is a creative project you want to launch, practice refusing as many distractions as you can, and you will gradually build the power required to drive it forward.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 창의적인 작업을 하려면 방해 요소를 최대한 거절해야 한다.
창의력은 다양한 사람들과 자주 어울릴 때 커진다.
꽃을 관찰하는 습관이 글쓰기 실력을 높여 준다.
업무상 점심 모임은 경력 관리에 꼭 필요하다.
창의적인 일은 짧은 시간에 끝내는 것이 효과적이다.
items.exp: 창의적 프로젝트를 시작하려면 가능한 한 많은 방해 요소를 거절하는 연습을 하라고 주장하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 오키프는 거대한 꽃 그림으로 유명한 미국 화가이다.
글쓴이는 부동산 업계에서 여러 해 일한 적이 있다.
글쓴이는 점심 식사와 글쓰기를 함께 하는 것이 쉽다고 느꼈다.
글쓴이는 창의력을 위해 업무 생활을 단순하게 바꿨다.
글쓴이는 창작 과정을 증기 기관에 비유했다.
items.exp: 글쓴이는 글쓰기와 사람들과의 점심 식사가 전혀 어울리지 않는다는 걸 알게 됐다고 했어요.

items.q: 글쓴이가 점심 모임과 여러 초대를 거절하게 된 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 건강을 위해 식사량을 줄이기로 해서
글이 탄력을 받은 뒤 식사로 쉬면 그날 글쓰기가 끝나 버려서
부동산 업계를 완전히 떠나고 싶어서
동료들과 사이가 좋지 않아서
오키프의 조언을 직접 들어서
items.exp: 작업에 탄력이 붙은 뒤 식사를 위해 멈추면 그날의 글쓰기가 끝나 버렸기 때문에 습관을 바꿨다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에 쓰인 단어 momentum의 영영 풀이로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a short period of rest
a feeling of deep regret
a meeting held over a meal
a written plan for the future
the force that keeps something moving forward

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? "Creative work resembles a steam engine: getting its wheels ___ demands enormous inner energy and resources."
choices: turn
turns
to turning
to turn
being turn

items.q: 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: Georgia O'Keeffe's Flower Paintings
The Joy of Business Lunches
Protect Your Time: Say No to Distractions
How Steam Engines Changed Industry

Truly seeing a flower takes time.
Artists should eat lunch alone.
Creativity cannot be taught.
Huge paintings sell better than small ones.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Creativity, like truly seeing a flower, needs (A) ___ time, so the writer simplified his working life by refusing invitations, and he advises others to (B) ___ distractions in order to build creative power.

(A) shared — (B) avoid
(A) protected — (B) welcome

(A) shared — (B) welcome
items.exp: 'That time, however, must be protected'이고, 'practice refusing as many distractions as you can'이라고 조언했어요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (That time, however, must be protected from the countless ___ we so readily let control our days.)
choices: opportunities
memories
compliments
distractions

units.name: 90 Comprehending Societies
units.passage: How much history matters to the social sciences differs greatly depending on the case. Yet the very idea that its importance varies is a historical claim, and it has to be argued and examined using historical evidence. Consider the United States. Because the country never went through a feudal period, many of its characteristics took shape, such as its complicated, many-sided elite and the remarkable ease with which people move up and down the social ladder. This mobility is frequently mistaken for a total absence of social classes or of awareness of class. Faced with such complicated examples, numerous social scientists have turned away from history, relying on a range of methods instead. Regrettably, these efforts force them to adopt assumptions about history and society that are both unhelpful and incorrect. When researchers abandon history in this way, they lose any chance of accurately grasping even the newest aspects of a society. Even for present-day America, the claim that history does not matter can all too easily be taken to an extreme.

items.q: 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: why social classes disappeared in modern America
the need for historical context to understand present-day societies
new research methods that replace historical study
the political system of the feudal period in Europe
differences between American and European elites
items.exp: 역사에서 물러나면 사회의 가장 현대적인 특징조차 정확히 이해할 수 없다며, 사회 이해에 역사적 맥락이 필요하다고 말하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 역사가 사회과학에 갖는 중요성은 모든 경우에 똑같다.
미국은 봉건 시대를 거친 뒤 지금의 사회 구조를 갖추었다.
미국 사회에서는 계층 간 이동이 매우 어렵다.
미국의 높은 계층 이동성은 계급이 전혀 없는 것으로 오해되곤 한다.
글쓴이는 역사를 외면한 사회과학자들의 방법이 정확하다고 본다.
items.exp: 계층 간 이동이 쉬운 특성이 계급이나 계급 의식이 전혀 없는 것으로 자주 오해된다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에 따르면, 사회과학자들이 역사를 외면했을 때 생기는 결과로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 생산적이지도 정확하지도 않은 가정을 세우게 된다.
봉건 시대에 대한 연구가 더 활발해진다.
미국 엘리트층의 특징을 더 정확히 파악하게 된다.
다양한 연구 방법을 쓸 수 없게 된다.
사회 계급에 대한 오해가 사라진다.
items.exp: 역사를 피하려는 시도 때문에 역사와 사회에 대해 도움이 되지도 정확하지도 않은 가정을 세우게 된다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에 쓰인 단어 mobility의 영영 풀이로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the act of traveling to another country
the use of portable electronic devices
the ability of people to move between social positions
a strong desire to keep old traditions
a sudden change in the weather
items.exp: 앞 문장의 '사회적 사다리를 오르내리는 쉬움'을 가리키므로 사회적 지위 간 이동 가능성을 뜻해요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은? "...such as its complicated, many-sided elite and the remarkable ease ___ people move up and down the social ladder."
choices: with which
which
with what
whom
with that
items.exp: '쉽게(with ease)' 이동한다는 의미이고 뒤 절이 완전하므로 전치사를 앞세운 with which가 알맞아요. that은 전치사 뒤에 쓸 수 없어요.

items.q: 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: The End of Social Classes in America
Why History Still Matters to Social Science
Feudalism: Europe's Forgotten Past
New Methods Make History Unnecessary
How to Climb the Social Ladder
items.exp: 역사를 버린 연구자는 'lose any chance of accurately grasping even the newest aspects of a society'라며 역사의 중요성을 말하는 글이에요.

items.q: What does the passage say about the claim that history's importance varies from case to case?
choices: It proves that history can be safely ignored.
It was first made by American social scientists.
It is itself a historical claim that must be examined with historical evidence.
It applies only to feudal societies.
It has been rejected by most researchers.
items.exp: 'the very idea that its importance varies is a historical claim, and it has to be argued and examined using historical evidence'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Although history's role in the social sciences (A) ___ by case, social scientists who turn away from it end up with faulty assumptions and (B) ___ to understand even the most recent features of a society.
choices: (A) varies — (B) fail
(A) varies — (B) manage
(A) stays fixed — (B) fail
(A) grows — (B) learn
(A) stays fixed — (B) manage
items.exp: 역사의 중요성은 'differs greatly depending on the case'이지만, 역사를 버리면 'they lose any chance of accurately grasping even the newest aspects of a society'라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [can all too easily be taken to an extreme]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Even for present-day America, the claim that history does not matter can all too easily be taken to an extreme.)
choices: 미국 역사는 극단적인 사건으로 가득하다
역사 연구는 극소수의 학자만 할 수 있다
현대 미국은 역사를 매우 중시한다
역사가 중요하지 않다는 주장이 너무 쉽게 지나친 수준까지 밀려갈 수 있다
역사의 중요성을 입증하기가 극도로 쉽다
items.exp: 'the claim that history does not matter'가 주어이고, 그 주장이 지나치게 극단으로 치우치기 쉽다는 경고예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: How much history matters to the social sciences [differs] greatly
it has to be argued and examined using historical [evidence]
This mobility is frequently [mistaken] for a total absence

items.exp: 역사를 버리면 사회의 새로운 측면을 '정확하게(accurately)' 파악할 기회를 잃는다는 문맥이므로 inaccurately는 맞지 않아요.
